faculty.lab: Computer Vision Lab (co-directed with Erik Learned-Miller); personal group page at people.cs.umass.edu/~smaji/group.html
faculty.research_areas: High-level visual recognition, fine-grained and hierarchical classification, structured prediction, AI for science (ecology, remote sensing, astrophysics), asymmetric/hierarchical task relationships via box embeddings.
faculty.why_match: Maji's 'Task2Box: Box Embeddings for Modeling Asymmetric Task Relationships' (CVPR 2024) encodes hierarchical/asymmetric structure geometrically rather than as a post-hoc correction - the same design philosophy as HiME's chain-rule decoding of per-level conditional sigmoids, which makes the upward-closed prediction set a theorem (Prop. 1) rather than a measured property. Akshat's ablation showing the structural constraint is a small accuracy tax under a frozen encoder but free under a fine-tuned one (frozen HiME 0.858 vs flat 0.888; fine-tuned HiME 0.952) is exactly the kind of representation-vs-constraint tradeoff Maji's group studies when comparing structured embedding spaces to flat ones. His recent AI-for-science work (WildSAT, RiverScope) also mirrors Akshat's applied, data-centric-ML instinct (interest A).
faculty.key_paper_1: Task2Box: Box Embeddings for Modeling Asymmetric Task Relationships. CVPR, 2024.
faculty.key_paper_2: WildSAT: Learning Satellite Image Representations from Wildlife Observations. ICCV, 2025. (See also: Active Measurement: Efficient Estimation at Scale, NeurIPS 2025.)
faculty.taking_students: Unstated explicitly for Fall 2027, but strong circumstantial evidence of an active, growing, well-funded lab: promoted to Full Professor 9/2025, new NSF grants 9/2025, multiple 2025-26 acceptances (NeurIPS'25, ECCV'26, ICML'26, UAI'26), Area Chair for NeurIPS'25. Verified 2026-08-28.
faculty.contact_policy: Not stated on the personal homepage (no explicit 'email me' or 'do not email' instruction found).
faculty.email_angle: Your Task2Box work encodes asymmetric hierarchy directly into the embedding geometry; I built a chain-rule decoding rule that makes hierarchical consistency a theorem rather than a trained property, and my own ablation shows that guarantee is free under a fine-tuned encoder but costs accuracy under a frozen one - I'd like to understand when embedding-level structure beats decoding-level structure.
faculty.notes: Best structural-methods match at UMass for HiME (interest D). Domain mismatch to flag honestly: his current output has shifted heavily toward ecology/remote-sensing/citizen-science applications rather than medical imaging; frame the pitch around the hierarchical-embedding METHOD, not the application domain.

faculty.research_areas: Hybrid models and deep learning methodology for multimodal biomedical data (time series, text, images); clinical outcome prediction (Alzheimer's onset, ICU mortality); machine learning for healthcare.
faculty.why_match: Fiterau's lab builds hybrid/fused models specifically for clinical prediction under label and modality scarcity - directly adjacent to Akshat's lumbar-spine semi-supervised pseudo-labeling work, where he showed MC-dropout uncertainty and confidence thresholding give comparable pseudo-label quality (0.7910-0.7922 mIoU) and that per-class thresholds calibrated on just 5 reference images matched thresholds derived from 304 (calibration-efficient uncertainty use). Her 'Dynamic Clustering via Branched Deep Learning Enhances Personalization of Stress Prediction from Mobile Sensor Data' (Nature Scientific Reports, 2024) and 'Augmenting Randomized Controlled Trials with Foundation Models as Synthetic Units' (2025) both use generative/synthetic data to compensate for scarce real clinical data - the same problem Akshat's A-PDF (cWGAN-GP + post-hoc distributional plausibility filter for synthetic lumbar-spine masks) tackles from the discriminative-filtering side.
faculty.key_paper_1: Dynamic Clustering via Branched Deep Learning Enhances Personalization of Stress Prediction from Mobile Sensor Data. Nature Scientific Reports, vol. 14, no. 6631, 2024.
faculty.key_paper_2: Augmenting Randomized Controlled Trials with Foundation Models as Synthetic Units. ACM (proceedings, no. 32), 2025. (See also: Experimentation under Treatment Dependent Network Interference, UAI 2025.)
faculty.taking_students: Unstated explicitly for Fall 2027 on the personal/lab pages checked this pass; lab publication record is active through 2025, suggesting an ongoing, funded group. Verified 2026-08-28.
faculty.contact_policy: Not stated (personal page has a generic 'CONTACT ME' mailto link, no screening instructions).
faculty.email_angle: My spine-MRI pseudo-labeling work found that MC-dropout uncertainty and confidence thresholding produce nearly identical pseudo-label quality and that thresholds calibrated on 5 reference scans match those from 304 - I'd like to work on when cheap uncertainty proxies are 'good enough' as filters for synthetic or fused clinical data, which is the question your synthetic-RCT-units work is asking from the generative side.
faculty.notes: Directory listing shows title 'Ina Fiterau Brostean'; personal site uses 'Madalina Fiterau.' Best healthcare/uncertainty-filtering match at UMass (interests B, C). No explicit prospective-student notice found - status genuinely unstated, not confirmed open or closed.

faculty.lab: Computer Vision Lab (co-directed with Subhransu Maji)
faculty.research_areas: Computer vision (face/object detection and recognition, motion segmentation), self-training and domain adaptation, structured prediction combining CRFs with learned shape priors, confidence intervals and uncertainty for bounded random variables, facial recognition policy/ethics.
faculty.why_match: Learned-Miller's 'Automatic adaptation of object detectors to new domains using self-training' (CVPR 2019) uses high-confidence detections plus hard-example mining via tracking to generate pseudo-labels for retraining - structurally the same self-training loop Akshat ran for spine MRI (confidence + uncertainty-filtered pseudo-labels lifting a teacher 0.7349 to a student 0.8162 mIoU). His 'A New Confidence Interval for the Mean of a Bounded Random Variable' builds principled uncertainty bounds without distributional assumptions, directly relevant to Akshat's MC-dropout uncertainty filtering. His older 'Augmenting CRFs with Boltzmann Machine Shape Priors' work - combining a local CRF with a global RBM shape prior - is an earlier example of imposing structure on a prediction (parallel to HiME's chain-rule-decoded hierarchy).
faculty.key_paper_1: Automatic adaptation of object detectors to new domains using self-training. CVPR, 2019.
faculty.key_paper_2: A New Confidence Interval for the Mean of a Bounded Random Variable. arXiv:1905.06208 (technical report/preprint).
faculty.taking_students: Unstated on personal homepage this pass; as Chair of the Faculty since 2022 his administrative load is heavy, and his publication list on the personal site appears not updated with very recent (2024-2026) work - status genuinely unclear.
